title: EvalResultV1
description: The output of one eval run, committed to eval/results/ so the run history is part of the record. Carries enough provenance to reproduce the run and to explain a number that moved: git SHA, prompt versions, model ids, price table date, and the fixture set hash.

mode.description: replay reads recorded provider responses from disk and makes zero network calls, which is what makes the eval CI-gateable. live makes paid calls and is a manual operation.

item_count.description: How many benchmark questions this run covered

criteria.description: Declarative exit criteria evaluated for this run. CI fails on a regression below the floor, not on a fixed target.

passed.description: True when every criterion held. The eval runner exits non-zero when this is false.

git_sha.description: Commit the runtime was built from

fixture_set_hash.description: Hash of the recorded provider responses used. Re-running an old fixture set after a prompt change shows exactly what moved.

price_table_date.description: Date the price table behind the dollar figures was last verified

models.description: Model ids in play, cheap tier first

prompt_versions.description: Prompt name to version, e.g. generate_sql -> v2

execution_accuracy.description: The headline number: fraction of questions whose result set matches gold

schema_recall_at_k.description: Fraction of questions whose retrieved subset contained every table in the gold query. Reported separately from execution accuracy so retrieval failures are distinguishable from generation failures — the single most useful diagnostic in the system.

k.description: The k that schema_recall_at_k was measured at

valid_sql_rate.description: Fraction of generations the guard accepted

repair_lift.description: Execution accuracy with repair minus accuracy without. May be negative, and a negative value is reported rather than hidden.

escalation_rate.description: Fraction of questions routed to the expensive tier

escalated_slice_accuracy.description: Accuracy on the escalated questions only. Compared against what the cheap tier alone scored on that same slice, this answers whether escalation actually pays.

abstention_rate.description: Fraction of questions the agent declined to answer

cost_per_correct_usd.description: Total dollars divided by correct answers

cache_false_hit_rate.description: Fraction of cache hits that returned SQL for a question it does not actually answer. The important cache number, and the one a naive hit-rate metric hides.

metric.description: Name of the metric this criterion gates

value.description: The measured value this run produced

description.description: Human-readable statement of the criterion, printed by the runner
